pages.title: A Master’s Signature
pages.text: Hit a hostile mob with Kusabimaru’s Dragon Flash or Ghiza’s Wheel’s innate dash. One technique is enough.

pages.title: A Master’s Signature
pages.text: Two native alloys support the next Nightfall weapon school; weapons and skills remain earned through their own progression.

pages.title: Getting started
pages.text: In battle mode, grounded Kusabimaru uses Dragon Flash through its assigned special input; airborne and dash contexts use other moves. Ghiza’s Wheel uses the weapon-innate-skill key; holding continues the attack and drains stamina. Read the weapon’s actual binding names, then find its native recipe

pages.title: Kusabimaru: context changes the move
pages.text: Kusabimaru’s assigned special input gives Dragon Flash on the ground, Sakura Dance in the air, Shadow Rush during a dash and double Ichimonji while sneaking. Use the current mapped input. An enhanced art from a separate missing expansion is not part of this profile.

pages.title: The wheel: prepare bleeding
pages.text: Ghiza’s Wheel basic attacks build bleeding; its innate dash then uses those accumulated effects. Holding continues the spin and spends stamina. Build a short series, then dash instead of holding without regard to stamina.

pages.title: Yamato: three move sets
pages.text: In Yamato’s tooltip A means the mapped basic input and S the mapped special input, not the literal S key. Basic style has grounded chains, held Judgement Cut and aerial moves. Separate mapped Angel/Demon controls change the move set: Angel emphasizes rapid slashes, rising attacks and aerial orbit;

pages.title: Yamato: three move sets
pages.text: Demon uses heavier chains, launches and descending attacks. Direction and holding alter follow-ups.

pages.title: Yamato: phantom swords and double
pages.text: Phantom swords and Doppelganger have separate bindings. Style determines teleporting to a target or pulling it; movement direction selects attacks, while sneaking selects Spiral or enchanted Heavy Rain. Their bars are real costs shown by the native tooltip. Other enchants add protection and

pages.title: Yamato: phantom swords and double
pages.text: automatic swords. Judgement Cut End needs its learned skill; the native kill-reward setting controls its unlock, and quests do not grant it early.

pages.title: Murasama: draw and stance
pages.text: Murasama X/Y stand for mapped basic/special inputs. A basic sequence followed by special chooses a follow-up; holding special selects a charged form. A separate sheath control changes sprint attacks. Sneaking and direction alter draws and counters; taunt also uses a sheath-key combination. Follow

pages.title: Murasama: draw and stance
pages.text: the current weapon tooltip rather than somebody else’s keyboard layout.

pages.title: Blade Mode and Zandatsu
pages.text: A learned Blade Mode is specific to HF-Murasama: hold the assigned art input and spend weapon charge. Mouse direction selects the slash plane; a tap makes one slash and holding repeats it. An additional input mode uses eight mouse directions. Enough hits or low target health enables the native

pages.title: Blade Mode and Zandatsu
pages.text: Zandatsu finisher; merely entering the mode does not execute the finisher.

pages.title: Mortal Blade: a separate art
pages.text: Mortal Blade is a separately learned art with its own binding, stamina cost, stacks and cooldown. The normal class defaults are 3 stamina, 3 stacks and 30 seconds; active skill data may override those values, so the current skill tooltip is authoritative. Extra combinations from an enhancement addon

pages.title: Mortal Blade: a separate art
pages.text: require that addon to be installed.
